newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ASPRILLA DOUBLE STRIKE SETTLES NEWCASTLE NERVES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ASPRILLA DOUBLE STRIKE SETTLES NEWCASTLE NERVES.

text.p: Colombian Faustino Asprilla hit two late goals in as many minutes to steer nervous Newcastle past French team Metz and into the UEFA Cup quarter-finals on Tuesday.
Newcastle, who drew the first leg of the third-round tie 1-1 in France, won the second leg 2-0 to go through 3-1 on aggregate.
Metz battled bravely and held out until the 80th minute when Asprilla broke through to settle the home team's nerves.

However, there was also double disappointment for Asprilla, who was booked for an over-elaborate celebration of his first goal, the Colombian rushing over to the touchline and flinging his shirt over the corner flag before waving it at supporters.
The yellow card means that Asprilla, who was booked in the first leg, will miss the first leg of next March's quarter-final tie.
Moreover, the Colombian was carried off the field on a stretcher two minutes from the end with an injured hamstring.
Asprilla fired Newcastle ahead when he stooped to head home Darren Peacock's cross at the near post.

Within two minutes, Newcastle's UEFA Cup specialist -- he has scored his five goals this season in the competition -- raced clear from the halfway line and chipped over advancing Metz goalkeeper Andre Biancarelli.
It was rough justice for Metz who, inspired by Robert Pires, carved out the better chances and were only let down by wayward finishing.
